 Eastern New Mexico 
 Severe storms could bring damaging winds, large hail and heavy rain to the region late this evening and overnight, with a Level 2 of 5 (slight) risk in place.
 The main threats include damaging wind gusts up to 75 mph and large hail. Heavy rain could fall at rates up to 2 inches per hour, creating isolated flash-flood concerns. Tornadoes are possible, although the threat is low. Any tornado that develops could become strong.
 RELATED: Track severe storms using the Storm Search 7 Radar 
 Storms could begin as early as 8 p.m. MT in eastern New Mexico and move east, potentially reaching Amarillo around midnight to 1 a.m. CT. Storms may continue across the Panhandles into the early morning hours.
 Because the storms are expected at night, any tornadoes may be difficult to see. Residents are urged to charge devices, keep alerts on and have a plan. If a severe thunderstorm or tornado warning is issued, people should take shelter immediately. Additional updates are expected through the night.
 If you capture severe weather or storm damage, upload your photos and video at abc7amarillo.com/chimein .
